html:
The parliament building of Bangladesh in Dhaka, designed by the American architect Louis Kahn and built from 1961 to 1982. It is one of the great buildings of the 20th century.

It was commissioned by the government of Ayub Khan when Bangladesh was East Pakistan, as a second seat of Pakistan's national assembly. Work stopped during the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971 and resumed for the new country. Kahn died in 1974 and never saw it finished; it opened in 1982.

The building is a cluster of massive concrete forms banded with marble, set in an artificial lake. Huge geometric openings, circles, triangles and squares cut through the walls, bring in light and keep out the heat, recalling old forts and mosques without copying them. At its heart is the assembly chamber under a high roof that filters daylight. Together with Chandigarh, it is the best known example of modernist architecture in South Asia.
sum: The parliament building of Bangladesh in Dhaka, designed by the American architect Louis Kahn and built from 1961 to 1982. It is one of the great buildings of the 20th century.
